INDUSTRY.title: Industry & metallurgy
INDUSTRY.axis: Ore → Iron Ingot → Refined Iron Ingot; Scrap → Machine Parts → Gear / Pipe / Plate / Blade. Parts (found, never crafted) pays for knowledge and technology.

BUILDING.title: Building
BUILDING.axis: Wood → Stone → Brick → Iron (Glass for windows, Rope for fittings, Iron Plate for patching).

POWER.title: Power & automation
POWER.axis: Solid fuel (Wood → Charcoal → Coal → Briquette) heats stations; Fuel Canister runs generators; packed devices are built from Iron + Machine Parts + Parts.

TRANSPORT.title: Transport
TRANSPORT.axis: Hand Cart (wood + iron) → Utility Motorbike (Frame + Drive + Plates), run on Fuel Canister, serviced with Lubricant.

GEAR.title: Tools, weapons & worn gear
GEAR.axis: Stone/wood starter → Iron tier → Salvager tier (iron tool + Machine Parts + Parts); hide → Leather → armour; Canvas → pack and canteen.

FARMING.title: Farming
FARMING.axis: Wild Seeds / Bitterleaf → Garden Plot → Sunroot / Bitterleaf → cooked food and Fodder.

HUSBANDRY.title: Husbandry
HUSBANDRY.axis: Taming Lead + feed → penned animal → renewable product (egg, feather, fur, hide, meat).

SURVIVAL.title: Survival & medical
SURVIVAL.axis: Raw food → Campfire meal (hunger / thirst / warmth / health trade-offs); Fiber → Bandage → Medkit; Gland → Purge Tonic; water containers.

CORE.title: Creator Core
CORE.axis: Core (the weapon) + Basic / Refined Energy (the ammunition) + one Essence (the Signature fuel).

SPECIAL.title: Special, Elder & Ragnarok
SPECIAL.axis: Blueprints and specimens teach recipes; keycard opens vaults; Elder stones, relics, Ragnarok cash and the Escrow Chest carry the run objective.

options.title: Two distinct axes
options.summary: `spares` is shown as Parts and stays the uncraftable progression resource. `mechanical_parts` is shown as Machine Parts, a crafted component. Gear / Pipe / Plate / Blade keep their ids and have one clear job each (P3–P5, implemented in round 2). Fasteners stay a separate researched joining stock (P2 ruled out).

scores.implementation_cost: Small: two display names, two recipe revisions and one new Recycler rule (all done in round 2).
scores.clarity: High: one word, one item. "Parts are found; Machine Parts are made."
scores.gameplay_choice: Kept: Parts still competes between research, trade, Cores and devices (Bible K4).
scores.scarcity: Unchanged: no new Parts source, no craft recipe.
scores.exploit_risk: None added: the research currency still cannot be crafted.
scores.save_compatibility: Full: no id or recipe changes in P1.

options.title: Collapse to a single Parts item
options.summary: Merge `mechanical_parts` into `spares` so there is one Parts item, as in Last Island. Every recipe that takes Machine Parts takes Parts instead.

scores.implementation_cost: Large: 22 consumer targets and 13 repair costs rewired, every Recycler return re-versioned, loot tables re-rolled, inventory conversion.
scores.gameplay_choice: Reduced: bulk machine-building and scarce research would draw on the same pool, so one starves the other.
scores.scarcity: Broken unless the Machine Parts recipe is deleted: today 2 Scrap + 1 Iron Ingot makes 2, i.e. 5 Scrap would buy 2 research Parts.
scores.exploit_risk: High. The live graph already contains a Parts-positive loop under a merge: an Iron Axe uses no Machine Parts but its Recycler rule returns one. Every such rule would have to be rewritten.
scores.save_compatibility: Risky: converting stacks changes the value of what players hold; in-flight jobs and versioned Recycler jobs need special cases.

recommendation.reason: Option A gets the clarity benefit for almost no cost and keeps the research currency uncraftable. Option B can only be made safe by deleting the Machine Parts recipe, rewriting every Recycler return and converting player inventories — a large migration whose end state is a single pool where building machines and buying knowledge fight each other. That removes a decision the Bible asks for (K4) rather than clarifying it.
